Replay the trained weights timestep-by-timestep, without fitting another model. PyTorch stores gate chunks in **reset, update, new** order. Compute `a=linear(x,W_ih,b_ih)` and `b=linear(h,W_hh,b_hh)`, split each into `(r,z,n)`, then `r=sigmoid(a_r+b_r)`, `z=sigmoid(a_z+b_z)`, `n=tanh(a_n+r*b_n)`, `h=(1-z)*n+z*h`. Include both bias tensors: the recurrent candidate bias belongs inside the reset multiplication. Large `z` retains the previous state. Replay every layer with its own parameters and native initial state. Interlayer dropout applies between layers, excluding the last; use evaluation mode for both native execution and replay. Training-mode parity requires identical dropout masks; matching seeds alone does not establish parity. [PyTorch GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html)

Recommended measurement protocol: use a small, fixed sample of public training histories under inference mode. Preserve native embedding transformations and padding execution exactly; zero embeddings can still produce nonzero states through biases. Exclude padding positions from gate statistics, reporting per-layer quantiles and fractions below 0.1/above 0.9. For left padding, read the final nonpadding index, never `count-1`. At selected valid positions, perturb one layer’s hidden state by a small normalized vector, then replay the identical suffix. Report `||h_perturbed−h_reference||/||delta||` versus subsequent valid steps, across several positions and directions. This measures local sensitivity; gate products alone omit recurrent feedback.

Before interpreting measurements, compare unperturbed replay against fused native sequence outputs, all layers’ final states, and model scores. Report maximum absolute/relative errors with explicit tolerances. Match device, dtype and precision settings; bitwise equality across fused and explicit computations is not guaranteed. Reject materially mismatched replay. [PyTorch numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)
